topic: Operator Precedence and Associativity in C++
explanation: Understanding operator precedence and associativity is crucial for writing correct and predictable C++ code.  Operator precedence determines the order in which operators are evaluated in an expression, while associativity specifies the direction of evaluation when operators of the same precedence are present.  Incorrectly understanding these can lead to subtle and hard-to-find bugs.  For example, forgetting that multiplication has higher precedence than addition can lead to unexpected results.  Best practice is to use parentheses to explicitly clarify the order of operations, improving readability and reducing the risk of errors, even when the precedence rules are well understood.
keywords: Operator precedence C++, C++ associativity, Order of operations C++
